scenes.section: Why use codes instead of words?

lines.raw: One doctor writes "sugar", another writes "DM-2", another writes "Type 2 diabetes mellitus".
lines.say: One doctor writes "sugar", another writes "D M 2", another writes "Type 2 diabetes mellitus".

lines.raw: A computer cannot tell these are the same.
lines.say: A computer cannot tell these are the same.

lines.raw: So the world agreed on a **code book** where every disease has exactly one code.
lines.say: So the world agreed on a code book where every disease has exactly one code.

scenes.section: Why use codes instead of words?

lines.raw: That code book is the **ICD**, the **International Classification of Diseases**, created by the World Health Organization (WHO).
lines.say: That code book is the I C D, the International Classification of Diseases, created by the World Health Organization (W H O).

lines.raw: The US uses its own detailed version called **ICD-10-CM** (CM = Clinical Modification).
lines.say: The U S uses its own detailed version called I C D 10-CM (C M = Clinical Modification).

lines.raw: It has around **70,000+ codes**.
lines.say: It has around 70,000+ codes.

scenes.section: Why use codes instead of words?

lines.say: Nepal already uses I C D.

lines.raw: With private insurance:

lines.raw: Hospitals in Nepal use **WHO's ICD-10** to report diseases to the government health information system (HMIS).
lines.say: Hospitals in Nepal use WHO's I C D 10 to report diseases to the government health information system (H M I S).

lines.raw: So when you see the US code for typhoid, it belongs to the same family of codes Nepali hospital record officers use.
lines.say: So when you see the U S code for typhoid, it belongs to the same family of codes Nepali hospital record officers use.

lines.say: When a hospital sends a claim to S S F, it records the diagnosis: what disease Sita was treated for.

lines.raw: SSF uses the diagnosis to check that the treatment makes sense for that illness, and whether it falls under a special category such as serious illness.
lines.say: S S F uses the diagnosis to check that the treatment makes sense for that illness, and whether it falls under a special category such as serious illness.

lines.raw: Reading an ICD-10-CM code.

scenes.section: Reading an ICD-10-CM code

lines.raw: ICD-10-CM codes are **3 to 7 characters** long.
lines.say: I C D 10-CM codes are 3 to 7 characters long.

lines.raw: They always start with a **letter**, and there is a **dot after the 3rd character**.
lines.say: They always start with a letter, and there is a dot after the 3rd character.

lines.raw: The first 3 characters are the **category** (the general disease); the characters after the dot add detail.
lines.say: The first 3 characters are the category (the general disease); the characters after the dot add detail.

scenes.section: Reading an ICD-10-CM code

lines.raw: Simple code: strep throat.
lines.say: Simple code: strep throat.

lines.raw: J: Chapter: diseases of the **respiratory system** (breathing).
lines.say: J: Chapter: diseases of the respiratory system (breathing).

lines.raw: 02: Category: **acute pharyngitis** (sore throat).
lines.say: 02: Category: acute pharyngitis (sore throat).

lines.raw: .0: Detail: caused by **streptococcus** bacteria.
lines.say: .0: Detail: caused by streptococcus bacteria.

scenes.section: Reading an ICD-10-CM code

lines.raw: Detailed code: broken wrist.
lines.say: Detailed code: broken wrist.

lines.raw: S52: Category: **fracture of the forearm**.
lines.say: S52: Category: fracture of the forearm.

lines.raw: .5: Location: **lower end of the radius** (near the wrist).
lines.say: .5: Location: lower end of the radius (near the wrist).

lines.raw: 0: Type: **unspecified** fracture type.
lines.say: 0: Type: unspecified fracture type.

lines.raw: 1: Side: **right** arm.
lines.say: 1: Side: right arm.

lines.raw: A: Visit: **initial encounter** (first treatment) for a closed fracture.
lines.say: A: Visit: initial encounter (first treatment) for a closed fracture.

scenes.section: Reading an ICD-10-CM code

lines.raw: Common ICD-10-CM codes with familiar illnesses.
lines.say: Common I C D 10-CM codes with familiar illnesses.

lines.raw: `A01.00`. Meaning: Typhoid fever, unspecified. Where you'd see it in Nepal: Very common, especially in summer and monsoon.
lines.say: A 0 1 . 0 0. Meaning: Typhoid fever, unspecified. Where you'd see it in Nepal: Very common, especially in summer and monsoon.

lines.raw: `A90`. Meaning: Dengue fever. Where you'd see it in Nepal: Outbreaks every monsoon season.
lines.say: A90. Meaning: Dengue fever. Where you'd see it in Nepal: Outbreaks every monsoon season.

lines.raw: `J02.0`. Meaning: Strep throat. Where you'd see it in Nepal: Sore throat with fever.
lines.say: J 0 2 . 0. Meaning: Strep throat. Where you'd see it in Nepal: Sore throat with fever.

lines.raw: `E11.9`. Meaning: Type 2 diabetes without complications. Where you'd see it in Nepal: "Sugar" patients in every OPD.
lines.say: E 1 1 . 9. Meaning: Type 2 diabetes without complications. Where you'd see it in Nepal: "Sugar" patients in every O P D.

lines.raw: `I10`. Meaning: High blood pressure (essential hypertension). Where you'd see it in Nepal: "Pressure" patients.
lines.say: I10. Meaning: High blood pressure (essential hypertension). Where you'd see it in Nepal: "Pressure" patients.

lines.raw: `K35.80`. Meaning: Acute appendicitis, unspecified. Where you'd see it in Nepal: Sita's appendix surgery.
lines.say: K 3 5 . 8 0. Meaning: Acute appendicitis, unspecified. Where you'd see it in Nepal: Sita's appendix surgery.

lines.raw: `R50.9`. Meaning: Fever, unspecified. Where you'd see it in Nepal: Fever where the cause is not yet known.
lines.say: R 5 0 . 9. Meaning: Fever, unspecified. Where you'd see it in Nepal: Fever where the cause is not yet known.

lines.raw: `Z00.00`. Meaning: General adult check-up, no abnormal findings. Where you'd see it in Nepal: Annual health check-up package.
lines.say: Z 0 0 . 0 0. Meaning: General adult check-up, no abnormal findings. Where you'd see it in Nepal: Annual health check-up package.

scenes.section: Reading an ICD-10-CM code

lines.raw: Letters give clues.
lines.say: Letters give clues.

lines.raw: **A–B** infections · **C** cancers · **E** hormones and diabetes · **I** heart and blood vessels · **J** lungs and breathing · **K** stomach and digestion · **R** symptoms · **S–T** injuries · **Z** check-ups and other reasons for a visit.
lines.say: A–B infections, C cancers, E hormones and diabetes, I heart and blood vessels, J lungs and breathing, K stomach and digestion, R symptoms, S–T injuries, Z check-ups and other reasons for a visit.

lines.raw: You do not need to memorise them all; just know codes are grouped by body system.
lines.say: You do not need to memorise them all; just know codes are grouped by body system.

scenes.section: Types of diagnoses on a claim

lines.raw: A patient can have more than one problem.
lines.say: A patient can have more than one problem.

lines.raw: A claim can carry **many diagnosis codes** (up to 12 on a CMS-1500, up to 25 on a UB-04).
lines.say: A claim can carry many diagnosis codes (up to 12 on a C M S 1500, up to 25 on a U B 04).

scenes.section: Types of diagnoses on a claim

lines.raw: Admitting diagnosis.
lines.say: Admitting diagnosis.

lines.raw: The problem the doctor writes **when the patient is admitted**, before tests confirm the cause.
lines.say: The problem the doctor writes when the patient is admitted, before tests confirm the cause.

lines.raw: Often just a symptom, like belly pain.
lines.say: Often just a symptom, like belly pain.

lines.raw: Used on **inpatient hospital claims** (UB-04), which have room for only **one** admitting code.
lines.say: Used on inpatient hospital claims (U B 04), which have room for only one admitting code.

lines.raw: Primary (principal) diagnosis.
lines.say: Primary (principal) diagnosis.

lines.raw: The **main reason** for the visit or hospital stay, confirmed after tests.
lines.say: The main reason for the visit or hospital stay, confirmed after tests.

lines.raw: Listed first.
lines.say: Listed first.

lines.raw: Secondary diagnoses.
lines.say: Secondary diagnoses.

lines.raw: Other conditions the patient has that affect care.
lines.say: Other conditions the patient has that affect care.

lines.raw: Example: Sita has appendicitis (primary) and also diabetes (secondary).
lines.say: Example: Sita has appendicitis (primary) and also diabetes (secondary).

lines.raw: Diagnosis pointer.
lines.say: Diagnosis pointer.

lines.raw: Sita's appendix stay: how the diagnoses change.
lines.say: Sita's appendix stay: how the diagnoses change.

lines.raw: Arrives at the hospital. Diagnosis type: Admitting. Code: `R10.31`. Meaning: Pain in the lower right belly (a symptom, cause not yet known).
lines.say: Arrives at the hospital. Diagnosis type: Admitting. Code: R 1 0 . 3 1. Meaning: Pain in the lower right belly (a symptom, cause not yet known).

lines.say: After tests and surgery. Diagnosis type: Principal. Code: K 3 5 . 8 0. Meaning: Acute appendicitis (the confirmed main reason).

lines.raw: Throughout the stay. Diagnosis type: Secondary. Code: `E11.9`. Meaning: Type 2 diabetes (another condition that affects her care).

lines.raw: Another example: Mr. Brown (60, has diabetes) is admitted with breathing trouble.
lines.say: Another example: Mr. Brown (60, has diabetes) is admitted with breathing trouble.

lines.say: Arrives with fever and breathing trouble. Diagnosis type: Admitting. Code: R 0 6 . 0 2. Meaning: Shortness of breath (a claim has only one admitting code, so the main symptom is chosen; the fever R 5 0 . 9 is noted in his chart).

lines.say: Found during the stay. Diagnosis type: Secondary. Code: J 1 2 . 8 2. Meaning: Pneumonia caused by C O V I D 19 (a new problem C O V I D caused).

lines.raw: Already had before. Diagnosis type: Secondary. Code: `E11.9`. Meaning: Type 2 diabetes (another condition that affects his care).
lines.say: Already had before. Diagnosis type: Secondary. Code: E 1 1 . 9. Meaning: Type 2 diabetes (another condition that affects his care).

scenes.section: Types of diagnoses on a claim

lines.raw: Where did the fever and breathing trouble go?
lines.say: Where did the fever and breathing trouble go?

lines.raw: Once COVID-19 is confirmed, the fever and shortness of breath are **not** coded again as secondary diagnoses.
lines.say: Once C O V I D 19 is confirmed, the fever and shortness of breath are not coded again as secondary diagnoses.

lines.raw: They are a normal part of COVID, so the COVID code already covers them.
lines.say: They are a normal part of C O V I D, so the C O V I D code already covers them.

lines.raw: **Secondary diagnoses** are for **other** conditions: a new problem (like pneumonia) or an illness the patient already had (like diabetes).
lines.say: Secondary diagnoses are for other conditions: a new problem (like pneumonia) or an illness the patient already had (like diabetes).

lines.raw: Symptoms are only coded when the cause is still unknown.
lines.say: Symptoms are only coded when the cause is still unknown.

scenes.section: Present on Admission (POA): did she have it when she arrived?

lines.raw: On an **inpatient** hospital claim, each diagnosis carries a small **Present on Admission (POA)** flag.
lines.say: On an inpatient hospital claim, each diagnosis carries a small Present on Admission (P O A) flag.

lines.raw: It answers one question: **did the patient already have this condition when she was admitted, or did it start in the hospital?**
lines.say: It answers one question: did the patient already have this condition when she was admitted, or did it start in the hospital?

scenes.section: Present on Admission (POA): did she have it when she arrived?

lines.raw: POA values in plain words.
lines.say: P O A values in plain words.

lines.raw: `Y`. Meaning: Yes, present when admitted. Sita's stay: Appendicitis, diabetes.
lines.say: Y. Meaning: Yes, present when admitted. Sita's stay: Appendicitis, diabetes.

lines.raw: `N`. Meaning: No, it started **during** the stay. Sita's stay: A wound infection after surgery would be `N`.
lines.say: N. Meaning: No, it started during the stay. Sita's stay: A wound infection after surgery would be N.

lines.raw: `U`. Meaning: Unknown: the records do not say. Sita's stay: -.
lines.say: U. Meaning: Unknown: the records do not say. Sita's stay: -.

lines.raw: `W`. Meaning: The doctor cannot tell clinically. Sita's stay: -.
lines.say: W. Meaning: The doctor cannot tell clinically. Sita's stay: -.

scenes.section: Present on Admission (POA): did she have it when she arrived?

lines.raw: Why POA matters for data.
lines.say: Why P O A matters for data.

lines.raw: A diagnosis with POA = `N` is a problem that began in the hospital, such as an infection or a fall.
lines.say: A diagnosis with P O A = N is a problem that began in the hospital, such as an infection or a fall.

lines.raw: Insurers and **Medicare** (the US government health plan for people aged 65 and over) use these flags to measure hospital safety and may pay less for some hospital-caused conditions.
lines.say: Insurers and Medicare (the U S government health plan for people aged 65 and over) use these flags to measure hospital safety and may pay less for some hospital-caused conditions.

lines.raw: Analysts filter on POA to separate "why she came in" from "what happened while she was there".
lines.say: Analysts filter on P O A to separate "why she came in" from "what happened while she was there".

lines.say: Medical necessity: the diagnosis must match the service.

lines.raw: Insurers check that the **why** supports the **what**.
lines.say: Insurers check that the why supports the what.

lines.raw: This is called **medical necessity**.

scenes.section: Key takeaways

lines.raw: Key takeaways.
lines.say: Key takeaways.

lines.raw: Diagnosis codes answer **why** the patient needed care.
lines.say: Diagnosis codes answer why the patient needed care.

lines.raw: The US uses **ICD-10-CM**: starts with a letter, 3–7 characters, dot after the 3rd.
lines.say: The U S uses I C D 10-CM: starts with a letter, 3–7 characters, dot after the 3rd.

lines.raw: Admitting diagnosis = first impression on admission.
lines.say: Admitting diagnosis = first impression on admission.

lines.raw: Principal diagnosis = confirmed main reason.
lines.say: Principal diagnosis = confirmed main reason.

lines.raw: Others are secondary.
lines.say: Others are secondary.

lines.raw: The **POA** flag on inpatient claims tells you whether a condition was there on arrival or started in the hospital.
lines.say: The P O A flag on inpatient claims tells you whether a condition was there on arrival or started in the hospital.

lines.raw: The diagnosis must support the service (medical necessity), or the claim can be denied.
lines.say: The diagnosis must support the service (medical necessity), or the claim can be denied.
